children: Canada's main stock index inched higher on Thursday, with gains in energy stocks offsetting the drag in financials as rising bond yields and oil prices kept investors wary of inflation and higher interest rates.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index
was up 0.24% at 35,125.61 points by 09:57 a.m. ET (1357 GMT), after logging its steepest one-day drop since June 5 on Wednesday.
Oil prices rose more than 4%, lifting the energy sector
1.8% and extending its yearly gains to nearly 50%, making it the best-performing major TSX sector in 2026
"TSX has benefited mostly from the conflict in the Middle East which has driven up oil prices," said Allan Small, senior investment advisor of the Allan Small Financial Group with iA Private Wealth
The heavily weighted financials sector (.SPTTFS) fell 0.5% as climbing yields reinforced expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose to 5.2796%, but was slightly below the multi-decade high it had scaled on Wednesday. Its Canadian counterpart (CA10YT=RR) rose on Thursday
"The number one negative right now is that yields are up," Small said
Elevated bond yields kept investors on edge as they reassessed the outlook for monetary policy and interest rates
Markets are pricing in at least one quarter-point rate hike from the Bank of Canada before the end of the year, according to data compiled by LSEG
Traders also expect one 25-basis-point interest rate hike from the US Federal Reserve before 2026 ends, according to LSEG data
edged up 0.8%, after touching a three-month low in the previous session as gold prices
jumped 11.9%, topping TSX after the specialty hardware distributor  reported a rise in third-quarter revenue
